title: The Prompt Payment Discount: What Two Percent Off Is Really Costing Your Margin
linkedin:
Most Australian SME owners have an early payment discount sitting on their invoice terms that nobody has costed in years.

Two percent off for payment in ten days instead of thirty feels harmless. It usually isn't.

Run the maths and trading two percent of an invoice's value for twenty days of earlier cash works out to an implied cost of money well above thirty percent a year. That's several multiples higher than what the same business would pay a bank for an overdraft covering the same gap.

It gets sharper once you look at margin instead of revenue. On a ten percent net margin, a two percent discount isn't costing two percent of revenue. It's costing a fifth of the profit sitting in that sale.

The reason it never gets flagged is simple. It's netted off the invoice before it hits the ledger, so it shows up as slightly lower revenue spread across hundreds of invoices rather than one visible cost anyone would question.

None of this means scrap the discount. Some businesses genuinely need faster cash and it's a fair price to pay. But it should be a decision made with the real cost in view, not a rate copied from an old template years ago and left alone.

Worth pulling your own terms out this week and running the number.

Full piece on the ProfitPulse blog. Link in the first comment.
